summary: Federated cross-cloud onboarding: Data Science segmented workspace IAM roles (AWS & GCP)
description: Issue summary: The Data Science org (ds-team) needs a federated onboarding path that grants temporary, least-privilege access to both AWS and GCP project resources for a segmented analytics workspace. Current problem: new hires and contractors are blocked from accessing the experiment cluster (k8s in GCP project redwood-ds-prod) and S3 buckets in the shared AWS analytics account because our existing cross-account roles were designed for full platform SRE access and are too permissive.
request_details: Requested outcome: 1) A pair of narrowly-scoped federation roles: one AWS cross-account role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodDS-FederatedReadWrite) with permission boundary limiting to specific buckets/prefixes and kms:Decrypt for ds-team KMS key; and one GCP Workload Identity pool binding that maps SAML/Okta groups to a GCP service account (redwood-ds-sa@redwood-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com) with iam.roles/iam.serviceAccountUser and roles/storage.objectViewer+roles/storage.objectCreator on gs://redwood-ds-artifacts. 2) A JIT (just-in-time) expiry of 8 hours for contractor sessions and 24 hours for full-time hires. 3) Audit hooks: CloudTrail (AWS) and Cloud Audit Logs (GCP) to stream to the security logging project with alerting when broad permissions are requested.
impact: Blocked onboarding for 6 DS hires and 2 contractors for the current sprint; several experiments delayed (estimated >40 engineer-hours lost). Security risk exists if teams circumvent by using SRE credentials.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) New DS engineer attempts terraform apply in redwood-ds-project using service account mapping. 2) IAM binding fails with 403 when accessing buckets. 3) Attempt to assume existing cross-account role returns access-denied because permission boundary disallows s3:PutObject to the requested prefix.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Security (Marcus Lee) confirmed existing AWS cross-account role (RedwoodPlatform-FullOps) is overly broad. Audit of CloudTrail shows three recent developer requests where engineers used SRE onboarding ticket to get temporary creds. GCP audit log shows missing workload identity provider mappings for the ds-team Okta group. Resource owners identified: aws-analytics-account (owner: Priya Rao), gcp-ds-project (owner: Lina Chen). We validated no current role exists matching the exact bucket prefixes required by DS experiments.
access_provisioning_plan: Planned steps: 1) Create AWS role RedwoodDS-FederatedReadWrite with a permissions boundary policy 'ds-perm-boundary' restricting to s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::redwood-ds-artifacts and prefixes 'experiments/*' and 'models/*', plus kms:Decrypt on alias/redwood-ds-kms. 2) Deploy Workload Identity Pool in GCP with mapping for Okta group 'okta:groups:ds-team' to redwood-ds-sa and grant storage.objectViewer/objectCreator on the specific bucket. 3) Implement automated session-duration enforcement via access token lifetime settings (AWS STS DurationSeconds and GCP access_token lifetime policy) defaulting to 8h for contractors and 24h for full-timers. 4) Add CloudWatch metric filter and GCP log-based metric to feed alerts to #security-iam channel. 5) Create a terraform module in terraform-iam repo and open PRs for review. 6) Run a staged rollout: first alpha to two engineers, then full ds-team if no issues in 48h.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-scoped policy may either block legitimate work or open data. Mitigation: Start with read-only binding on GS bucket and S3 then add PutObject after alpha. All changes will go through PR review and security sign-off. Enable temporary feature flag to allow emergency escalation via SRE-runbox only.
